text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- A minor error on the last bend cost Norwegian skater Roger Stroem the gold medal in the world sprint speed-skating championships in Hamar. He had to settle for silver behind Russian Sergei Klevchenya.

- Bishop Even Fougner in Borg wants traffic at Gardermoen airport to be halted during funeral ceremonies in seven nearby churches. Gardermoen will take over as Oslo's international airport from Fornebu in a few years.
- Alexander Oeyen, 17, was found alive and well after being buried for more than three hours under an avalanche at Harstad mountain in western Norway.
- Record catches of herring and mackerel were registered last year.
- Norwegian banks are expected to post solid profits for 1996 despite sharp competition in the financial market.
- Fred Olsen rig Borgland Dolphin will probably win a long-term contract with the State-owend Statoil oil company for drilling on the Norwegian shelf.
- Norwegian cod, cheese and aquavit will be offered to passengers on German trains this month as part of a campaign to draw tourists to Norway.
